why: next@16.3.3+ and sharp@0.35.4 cleared the two next RCE advisories (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36, GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4) and the sharp/libheif advisory (GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c) — real patch-version bumps, not baselined. maplibre-gl's GHSA-jrc7-96c5-q579 (DOM.sanitize() XSS in the attribution control, aka CVE-2026-85061) was previously baselined here because the installed 4.7.1 predated the vulnerable code (sanitize() was only added in 5.0.0, so 4.7.1 sat inside the advisory's stated '<= 6.4.0' range without containing the flaw). That baseline is gone as of 2026-09-23: maplibre-gl was bumped straight to 6.4.1, the actual fixed version, so the entry is removed rather than carried forward stale. 6.4.1 was chosen deliberately over any 5.0.0-6.4.0 version, since per the code-history analysis above those versions ARE genuinely vulnerable — re-verify this reasoning before ever downgrading maplibre-gl. picomatch (added 2026-11-17): GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf / CVE-2026-112366 (ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs, published 2026-10-19) covers every release <= 4.0.7, and 4.0.7 IS npm's dist-tag latest (published 2026-08-24) with no first_patched_version published — unlike the next/sharp/maplibre entries above, there is genuinely no version to move to, which is the only reason this workspace has a non-empty baseline again. The copy the gate counts is the production top-level picomatch@4.0.7; a second 2.3.2 nested under micromatch is dev-flagged and outside --omit=dev. Nothing depends on picomatch directly (it arrives via vite, @rollup/pluginutils, @rollup/plugin-commonjs, tinyglobby and @parcel/watcher — file-matching/build tooling) and no source file under src/ or app/ imports it. Accepted as unfixable, not as unreachable: whether any of those matchers ever sees attacker-controlled patterns is a security judgement this entry deliberately does not make. It self-expires — when a patched picomatch ships and the lockfile resolves it, the advisory stops being reported and the stale-entry check fails this gate until the entry is deleted.

Transitive only — reached through glob/file-matching tooling (vite, @rollup/pluginutils, @rollup/plugin-commonjs, tinyglobby, @parcel/watcher); no direct dependency and no src/app import of picomatch.
